subject: Use when reasoning about Test-Driven Development as a design discipline rather than a workflow: the red-green-refactor…

evals.prompt: Define test-driven-development in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the test-driven-development skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind test-driven-development. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "construct a mock, stub, or spy (use test-doubles-design)". Should test-driven-development activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force test-driven-development onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to eval-driven-development, type-safety, testing-strategy, test-doubles-design, refactor.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "explain why writing the test first changes the design of the code under test". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying test-driven-development.

Place test-driven-development among its adjacent skills (eval-driven-development, type-safety, testing-strategy, test-doubles-design, refactor). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about test-driven-development and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
